newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - July 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - July 29.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Telstra yesterday announced plans to acquire an equity stake in the AT&T World Partners global alliance. The deal will propel Telstra into the global telecommunications market and position it beside world telecommunications leaders like the Japanese intenational carrier KDD, Unisource of Europe and Singapore Telecom. Page 1.

Austrim chairman and chief executive Alan Jackson has announced a 300 per cent rise in profits and a double dividend for the year just ended. The news confirms Jackson's popularity with Austrim small shareholders. Page 1.

Federal Cabinet will today consider a Department of Finance plan which would require all departments and agencies involved in commercial activities to pay the equivalent of a 36 per cent company tax and a commercial dividend on their profits. The proposed changes are expected to increase the opportunities for private business to secure Commonwealth contracts. Page 3.

Federal Foreign Affairs Minister Alexander Downer yesterday announced the commencement of annual security dialogues with China, Vietnam, Thailand and the Philippines. The meetings will significantly strengthen Australia's strategic ties in East Asia and ill focus on regional security developments and the exchange of information on national security policies. Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Former Queensland Labor Premier Wayne Goss yesterday announced he would challenge One Nation leader Pauline Hanson for the seat of Oxley at the next Federal election. The move comes as the latest Newspoll reveals that One Nation has contained its recent fall in popularity and gained one percentage point, at the expense of the Australian Labor Party, to raise its level of support to seven per cent. Page 1.

A Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade spokesman confirmed yesterday that two Australian brothers serving life jail terms in Thailand for heroin smuggling had been granted royal pardons. The men, Paul Hudson, 45 and brother Noel, 40, have been release into the custody of Thai immigration officials and will be deported to Australia in the next few days. Page 1.

Former New South Wales detective Said Morgan accused of murdering a man who allegedly sexually assaulted three young girls related to him, has denied he took the law into his own hands. Morgan has admitted to the killing but claims he acted to protect the alleged victims of the man, who had threatened to kill them. Page 1.

Federal Industry Minister John Moore and Communications Minister Richard Alston will be unable to attend a special Federal Cabinet meeting on unemployment next Tuesday because of scheduled overseas trips. The absence of two key ministers has raised doubt as to the effectiveness of the meeting which have been reinforced by speculation that Prime Minister John Howard will also be unable to attend due to continuing illness. Page 2.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Federal Health Minister Michael Wooldridge has launched a national public awareness campaign as part of the Federal Government's Immunise Australia Program. Last night a television advertisement began screening which showed six-week-old Nathanial Eason truggling with a whooping cough attack. Page 1.

Sydney Harbour Casino head Neil Gamble and the Casino Control Authority will hold talks today with senior NSW police officers on what measures can be taken to stamp out loan-sharking at the Sydney Harbour Casino. Gamble has condemned loan-sharking and prmised to exclude from the casino any person found guilty of the activity. Page 1.

The New South Wales Attorney-General yesterday unveiled a plan to employ young people aged 17 to 23 as crime spotters. In a pilot project, to begin early next year, the young people will be called Community Safety Guides. The guides will be given train in and uniforms and they will patrol "risky" streets in one city suburb and one country town. Page 1.

New South Wales MP Sandra Nori is considering nominating for Australian Labor Party endorsement for the Federal seat of Sydney which will be vacated by Australian Labor Party long-timer Peter Baldwin at the next election. If Nori is successful the New South Wales Government will be forced to hold its first by-election since May last year when it won the seat of Clarence form the National Party. Page 2.
THE AGE

Melbourne's transport system has been paralysed this morning by a 24-hours strike that has stopped all trains, trams and most buses. Crisis talks last night between the Trades Hall Council secretary Leigh Hubbard and Public Transport Corporation head Ian Doobs and personal director Jim Carlisle failed to achieve a solution to the pay dispute. Page 1.

Long-term police corruption has been exposed in the Victorian rural town of Bright. Three internal reviews have confirmed that junior police attempted to discredit Senior Sergeant Mark Williams who was sent by Force Command to investigate allegations of corruption and violence made by the Bright community against local police. Page 1.

The Victorian State Government is considering a proposal to pay education welfare payments worth A$34 million directly to schools. The move will deny low income parents access to the education maintenance allowance and has been labelled a "de-facto" fundng increase to under-resourced schools by the Australian Education Union's state president Peter Lord. Page 1.

Federal Foreign Affairs Minister Alexander Downer said yesterday there was no reason to fear for the safety of thousands of Australians living in the Papua New Guinea capital Port Moresby. Downer was commenting on yesterday's rebellion by the Papua New Ginea defence force which has undermined the authority of Prime Minister Bill Skate. Page 1.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
